title: My Fair Lady
tagline: Mind your vowels and pass the cucumber sandwiches.
about: A cockney flower seller takes lessons from an arrogant professor of phonetics who bets he can pass her off as a lady.
cue: Serve the Scotch eggs when Alfred Doolittle turns up at Wimpole Street to see what his daughter is worth to the professor.
faces: London, 1912. Carriages at midnight.. Mind your vowels and pass the cucumber sandwiches.
I. Violets sold under the portico at Covent Garden.
II. Marbles in the mouth for elocution practice.
III. Black and white hats at Ascot.
Supper after the dancing. Duchesses at the top table, and the young lady nobody can place sits well away from the Hungarian.
Thin cucumber with whipped butter, cream cheese, dill and white pepper on soft white bread.
Jammy eggs in sage and nutmeg pork sausage meat, crumbed and fried golden, with piccalilli.
Seared beef fillet in mustard and mushroom duxelles wrapped in puff pastry.
Roasted golden with saffron and garlic. By George, she's got it.
Butter sponge layered with blackberry jam and vanilla cream.
Dry gin, elderflower cordial and lemon over ice, topped with soda, with cucumber ribbons and mint.
Eliza's aitch drill with Higgins, hurricanes and all.
At table: Eliza, who could have danced all night. Form BF 27. Poster and stills: TMDB.

    StartersMainsSweetsDrinks
    StartersAscot race day cucumber sandwichesThin cucumber with whipped butter, cream cheese, dill and white pepper on soft white bread, crusts off, in fingersHow to make it2 telegraph cucumbers, thinly sliced1/2 tsp salt100g butter, softened125g cream cheese, softened1/2 bunch dill, chopped1/2 tsp ground white pepper16 slices of soft white sandwich breadToss the cucumber with the salt and drain on paper towel.Beat the butter with the cream cheese, dill and white pepper.Spread the bread to the edges, lay cucumber over 8 slices and close with the rest.Press down gently, cut off the crusts and cut each into 3 fingers.Doolittle's pub Scotch eggsJammy eggs in sage and nutmeg pork sausage meat, crumbed and fried golden, with piccalilliHow to make it400g pork sausage meat6 eggs, 4 for boiling, 2 beaten1 tbsp chopped sage1 tsp English mustard1/2 tsp ground nutmeg1 tsp salt and pepper, to taste50g plain flour100g panko breadcrumbs1 L vegetable oil, for frying120g piccalilliLower 4 eggs into boiling water for 6 1/2 minutes, then into iced water. Peel.Mix the sausage meat with the sage, mustard, nutmeg, salt and pepper.Flatten a quarter of the mixture on wet hands, wrap it round an egg and seal. Chill 20 minutes.Roll each in flour, then the beaten eggs, then the panko.Deep-fry at 170°C for 7 minutes until deep golden and cooked through. Drain, halve and serve with piccalilli.MainsEmbassy Ball beef WellingtonSeared beef fillet in mustard and mushroom duxelles wrapped in puff pastry, with roast baby potatoes and green beansHow to make it1kg centre-cut beef fillet1 tbsp vegetable oil, for searing500g swiss brown mushrooms2 shallots, finely chopped2 cloves of garlic, crushed40g butter4 sprigs of thyme, leaves picked2 tbsp dijon mustard2 sheets of puff pastry1 egg, beaten2 tsp salt1 tsp ground black pepper750g baby potatoes300g green beans, trimmed2 tbsp olive oilSeason the beef with half the salt and pepper, sear all over in the vegetable oil in a very hot pan, brush with the mustard and cool.Blitz the mushrooms finely and cook with the shallots, garlic, thyme and butter until dry and dark. Cool.Lay the pastry sheets slightly overlapping, press to join, spread with the mushrooms, sit the beef on top, roll up and seal. Brush with egg and chill 20 minutes.Heat the oven to 200°C. Toss the potatoes with the olive oil and the rest of the salt and pepper and roast.Score the pastry and bake the Wellington for medium rare.Steam the beans for 4 minutes and rest the Wellington 10 minutes before slicing thickly.Rain in Spain saffron potatoesRoasted golden with saffron and garlic. By George, she's got itHow to make it1.2kg potatoes, cut in chunks1 pinch saffron threads50g butter2 tbsp olive oil4 garlic cloves, crushed1 small bunch parsleySoak the saffron in 2 tbsp hot water.Boil the potatoes for 8 minutes and drain well.Melt the butter with the oil, garlic and saffron water, toss through the potatoes and roast at 220°C until golden.Scatter with chopped parsley and salt.SweetsFlower girl's violet Victoria spongeButter sponge layered with blackberry jam and vanilla cream, under a pale violet lemon icing with edible flowersHow to make it200g butter, softened200g caster sugar4 eggs200g self-raising flour1 tsp vanilla extract2 tbsp milk200ml thickened cream160g icing sugar150g blackberry jam1 lemon, juiced1 drop purple food colouring1 punnet edible violas or violetsHeat the oven to 180°C and line two 20cm tins. Beat the butter and sugar until pale, then beat in the eggs one at a time.Fold in the flour, vanilla and milk, split between the tins and bake.Cool the sponges completely.Whip the cream with 1 tbsp of the icing sugar. Spread one sponge with jam, then cream, and top with the second.Mix the rest of the icing sugar with lemon juice and the food colouring, spread over the top and finish with the flowers.DrinksWimpole Street elderflower gin fizzDry gin, elderflower cordial and lemon over ice, topped with soda, with cucumber ribbons and mintHow to make it180ml dry gin80ml elderflower cordial2 lemons, juiced600ml soda water1 Lebanese cucumber, in long ribbons4 sprigs of mint3 cups iceFill 4 tall glasses with ice and add a couple of cucumber ribbons to each.Shake the gin, elderflower cordial and lemon juice with ice and strain into the glasses.Top with soda water and add a mint sprig.Chilled amontillado sherryEliza's aitch drill with Higgins, hurricanes and all.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
